score_basis: 105 caught / (105 caught + 20 demonstrated survivors) = 84.00%. The denominator excludes 8 mutants that DO NOT COMPILE (E0277 / E0369 -- a mutant no test can kill is excluded by definition). It INCLUDES every demonstrated survivor, including the 8 that are platform-unmeasured: excluding those (105/117 = 89.74%) and the one proven-equivalent mutant (105/124 = 84.68%) is offered as an additional reading, not as the headline. A survivor counts as missed unless the mutation is (a) provably equivalent with a written proof, or (b) decided caught by the re-check with a named failing assertion. Every verdict in all four runs is derived from its own per-mutant log (mutation/analyze-queue.py + mutation/dump-fails.py, mapping mutant -> log through outcomes.json because the log-file `_NNN` suffix is a run-order dedup counter, not the --list order). Zero verdicts are flake-driven: all four baselines were GREEN, and mutation/verify-attribution.py reports 0 catches whose only failing test is on the pre-fix flake list (and 0 that touch such a test at all for compat.rs). One caught verdict is non-deterministic and is flagged rather than smoothed over: compat.rs:360:61 was MISSED in the primary run and CAUGHT in the re-check by the same 150-round race witness.

uncaught.name: channels/src/bridge/queue.rs:220:26: replace < with > in Conversations::evict_idle
uncaught.verdict: MISSED by the tests, but no test can or should kill it -- excluded from the denominator
uncaught.reason: evict_idle is private with exactly ONE caller, Conversations::submit, which calls it with the locked table immediately before inserting exactly one entry. At that point entries.len() <= self.max_conversations is an invariant (the table starts empty; its only writers are evict_idle's own loop, which exits at len <= max - 1, and submit's single insert; get_mut replaces an existing entry without changing the size; with_limits consumes self so max_conversations can no longer change). entries.len() > self.max_conversations is therefore FALSE IN EVERY REACHABLE CALL -- both the original and the mutant return early on exactly the same condition.
uncaught.why_this_is_not_a_licence_to_weaken_anyt: the sibling mutants < -> == and < -> <= ARE caught (by the_table_evicts_instead_of_growing_without_bound and an_idle_conversation_is_evicted_and_its_worker_stops); only the > DIRECTION is dead. Nothing was deleted or weakened to obtain this exclusion.
uncaught.evidence: mutation/out-queue-full/mutants.out/log/... (no failing test); the killed siblings are in mutation/out-queue-full/mutants.out/caught.txt

uncaught.name: channels/src/bridge/queue.rs:232:54: replace > with >= in Conversations::evict_idle
uncaught.verdict: MISSED in both the stitched earlier measurement and this single complete measurement
uncaught.reason: Differs from the original ONLY when entry.last_used.elapsed() == self.idle_timeout exactly. For the only timeout a test can set (Duration::ZERO) that means reading last_used == Instant::now() inside evict_idle; production calls Instant::now() itself and injects no clock, so no test can construct that equality deterministically. Stated as a survivor rather than waived as equivalent, because the bytes DO differ on that input.
uncaught.what_to_add: nothing honest: an assertion cannot close this. It needs a clock seam (an injectable `now`) in production code, which is outside this item's write scope.

infrastructure_lessons: cargo-mutants' scratch tree is under %TEMP%, which is on C:. An earlier attempt died in 20 s at 16:13 with 'Failed to copy ... os error 112' (disk full) while C: had 0.1 GB free and D: had 246 GB. TEMP/TMP are pointed at D:\cov100-mut-tmp for every run.

A background child does not survive the agent's teardown of a tool call. Earlier attempts died that way with no outcome file. Every driver is now started through WMI Win32_Process.Create (mutation/run-*.cmd), so it is parented to WmiPrvSE and survives turn boundaries.

cargo-mutants' stdout is BLOCK-BUFFERED when redirected to a file: the run log stays at 3 lines while outcomes.json grows. Progress must be read from the output directory (last log mtime / outcomes.json), not from the log.

`--cargo-test-arg --lib` restricts cargo test to the lib target. For a crate that keeps its behaviour tests in tests/*.rs (future-loop), that silently produces witness-set misses. Add the integration targets that reference the file: `--cargo-test-arg --test --cargo-test-arg <name>`. This is a MEASURED effect here (12 of the 20 projection mutants would have been reported MISSED under a bare --lib).
`--json` does not disturb the outcome files; the authoritative mutant -> log map is always outcomes.json.
Useful: because cargo-mutants copies target/debug into its scratch tree, a per-mutant build is 13-100 s here instead of the ~92 s/mutant an earlier round measured with a cold shared target.
